title: Think Your Non-Compete Doesn’t Matter? Think Again.

 Think Your Non-Compete Doesn’t Matter? Think Again.
Hi Sara,
Let’s talk about the number one clause that gets glossed over, shrugged off, and misunderstood in nearly every deal I touch: the non-compete.
Every day, I hear some version of: “Non-competes aren’t enforceable, right? So who cares?”
Oh, just the buyer, the seller, the bank, and your entire deal. That’s who.
The Non-Compete Myth That Won’t Die
Thanks to headlines (and let’s be honest, a few clickbaity TikToks), people think non-competes are dead. But here’s the truth: they’re very much alive—especially when you’re buying or selling a business.
Even when the FTC tried to come for them, they carved out a big juicy exception for business sales. Why? Because you can’t buy an accounting firm and then let the seller open a competing firm across the street the next day. That's not a business deal. That's a mess.
Where Your Non-Compete Lives Matters
It’s not just what your non-compete says, but where it lives. Stick it in the wrong agreement—say, a consulting agreement instead of a purchase agreement—and you may find out the hard way it doesn’t hold up.
And don’t forget:
Geographic scope needs to be defined (50 miles from where, exactly?)

Time frame needs to make sense (hint: 5 years might not cover a 10-year SBA loan)

Actual clarity matters (your lawyer should be able to look at it and say, “Yes, you can do this” or “No, you absolutely cannot”)

But Wait, There’s More (Nuance)
Let’s say your seller still wants to do their grandkid’s taxes. Or help their favorite client until one of them dies (yes, that’s a real quote I’ve heard). That’s fine. Just write it down. Include exceptions. Carve it out. Make it clear.
Because a good non-compete shouldn’t feel like a straitjacket. It should feel like a well-fitting suit. Fits like a glove.
Want to stop treating your non-compete like fine print and start using it like a power move?

To smarter deals (and fewer legal regrets),
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder, Deal Academy
